title: Technology Sector Update for 05/29/2018: OKTA,VMW,ZTO,BABA,MOMO,AAPL
text:
Shutterstock photo Top Tech Stocks
MSFT -0.33%
AAPL -0.28%
IBM -1.75%
CSCO -0.67%
GOOG -1.42%
Technology stocks declined today, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 losing over 0.5% in value today while the Philadelphia semiconductor index also was posting a more than 0.6% retreat.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ Okta Inc ( OKTA ) climbed to a new, all-time high on Tuesday, rising 6% to a best-ever $54.99 a share, after analysts at Monness Crespi & Hardt initiated coverage of the cyber-security company with a Buy rating and a $59 price target. The move follows the company last week launching a new partnership with enterprise software firm VMware ( VMW ) to assist corporate clients with securely move to the cloud and better leveraging their existing technology investments. Okta last week also began a new initiative allowing Information Technology administrators to help employees secure data within various applications and services.
In other sector news:
+ Momo ( MOMO ) surged on Tuesday, racing as much as 13% higher, after the Chinese information technology company reported better-than-expected non-GAAP Q1 net income and revenue. Excluding one-time items, the comppany earned $0.69 per American depository share, up from $0.44 per ADS during the same quarter last year and beating the Capital IQ consensus by $0.19 per ADS. Total net revenue climbed to $435.1 million from $265.2 million during the year-ago period and also topping the $398.3 million analyst mean. Looking forward to the current quarter, the company is projecting a 51% to 55% increase in Q2 revenue over year-ago levels to a range of $470.0 million to $485.0 million compared the Street view modelling $429.8 million in Q2 revenue. The company's forecast includes around $4.5 million in revenue expected from its Tantan unit during June, which it expects to add to its Q2 financial results.
+ ZTO Express ( ZTO ) was more than 9% higher Tuesday afternoon, retracing most of a more than 12% advance to a best-ever $21.70 per American depository share that followed online retailer Alibaba ( BABA ) saying it was partnering with Cainiao to invest $1.38 billion in the Chinese delivery company. Alibaba is expecting the deal will see Cainiao and ZTO Express extend their current collaborations and also better embrace the New Retail concept developed by Alibaba promoting seamless integration between online and offline commerce. The investment also will support the focus by both Cainiao and ZTO on improving first- and final-mile pickup and delivery capabilities, warehouse management, cross-border logistics and technology-driven smart services, the companies said.
- Apple (AAPL) was narrowly lower in recent trade, bouncing off a brief jump on positive ground for the second time on Tuesday following reports the tech giant plans to use OLED screens on at least three of its iPhone models in 2019. The new phones are expected to come out during Apple's traditional September release window, according to MacRumors, citing a report in South Korea's Electronic Times.
